newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold to scrap dual-currency dividend.
newsitem.headline: Ahold to scrap dual-currency dividend.

text.p: Dutch supermarkets group Ahold NV said on Thursday it was dropping its policy of paying a dividend in two currencies: Dutch guilders and U.S. dollars.

"Partly in view of the the continuing internationalisation of Ahold, it has been decided to discontinue dividend declarations in two currencies; dividends as of the financial year 1997 will be declared in guilders only," it said.
"Cash dividends are based on a target pay-out ratio of approximately 40 percent," Ahold said.

Because interim dividends were paid out on new shares issued last July to finance the Stop & Shop acquisition in the United States, the 1996 pay-out ratio had exceeded this target ratio, but this was a lone exception to the rule, Ahold said.
